title: Roadblock Detection Fix Build Plan

approval: Build plan approved: roadblock detection fix

short.lead: A roadblock is any reason I give for stopping. The fix for it is built in three steps under parent issue #587. Step 1 is detection, step 2 is the evidence rule, and step 3 is never waiting in unattended or bypass mode. Check how I read your answers in the first card below, because I had to interpret two of them (answers 2 and 3).
short.hint: Tap a step to see it.
items: How I read your three answers

Answer 1: a first try never counts as "I can't". I try two different methods, and only then may I say something could not be verified, tested or done, and the reply lists every method tried. Answer 2: these nine phrases are always flagged: "can't verify", "won't verify", "unable to verify", "unable to", "could not", "couldn't", "don't have access", "not available here" and "isn't available". These four are flagged only in unattended or bypass mode: "not done", "I've stopped", "I've stopped here" and "next step". Answer 3: in those modes I make build-time design choices myself; I still wait for your approval before the build starts.
Tell me if a reading is wrong.

items.caption: My readings of answers 2 and 3 are interpretation, so check those two.

items: Step 1 makes the roadblock check match both straight (') and curly (’) apostrophes and adds the new phrases. It reads the session's permission mode, so the four stall phrases are flagged only in unattended or bypass sessions. It also makes the check block a reply twice. Today it never blocks twice: a second block is allowed, but the check exits as soon as it sees the retry.

items.caption: Step 1 changes the pattern that spots roadblock claims and the counter of how many times a reply was blocked.

items: A roadblock claim passes only when I tried two different methods on what the claim is about, both failed, and the reply lists each method. If I tried only one, the block asks for a second. A turn that only ran ls or git ls-files is blocked. If I cannot tell what the claim is about, any two failed tool results count. That fallback is a known weakness.

items.caption: Checking that a program exists, without trying to use it, no longer counts as evidence.

items: #590: never wait for you in unattended or bypass mode, plus docs, a version bump and a QA page

In unattended or bypass mode, a design decision is chosen, recorded and carried on. This adds one rule sentence, makes the hook that stops me asking questions (the no-questions hook) apply in bypass mode too, adds a check that blocks replies which hand you a decision to make, and posts a QA page for you to test the result.
Nothing from you until the QA page is posted. Then you test it.

items.caption: This rule applies only in unattended and bypass mode.

items: The build then starts with step 1, the detection fix (#588).
Reply "Build plan approved: roadblock detection fix".

changes: scripts/house_rules/core.py: the roadblock-claim pattern and the block counter
Step 1 widens detection and fixes the block count.

Done when: new verify.py test cases pass for each phrase with both straight and curly apostrophes. The stall phrases must fire only in unattended or bypass mode. A reply that retries must still be blocked a second time, but never a third.
Step 2 replaces the test that only checks whether a program exists with a test for two different failed methods, each listed in the reply.

Done when: a claim made after only git ls-files is blocked. A claim after a single failed Blender call asks for a second method. A claim after two different failed Blender calls, both listed in the reply, is accepted. The same claim with the methods left out of the reply is blocked.
show-dont-tell.md, the no-questions hook, and a new check that runs when I finish a reply (the Stop hook)
Step 3 stops waiting in unattended and bypass mode.

Done when: an unattended headless session that ends with "Your call" is blocked and carries on. The rules injected at session start must also stay under 9,700 characters when the plugin is installed at a path as long as the CI runner's, for example /home/runner/work/AjsClaudeCodeTools/AjsClaudeCodeTools.
